report.verdict: A "down 1%, up 2% underlying" quarter: revenue $990.5m (-1.4% YoY, ~1.1-1.3% below the ~$1.0bn consensus) and adj. EBITDAR $319.6m (-0.7%) were held up by Midwest & South (+2.5% adjusted), Online (+16%) and Managed (+13%), while the Las Vegas destination customer deteriorated further at the Orleans and Downtown (LV Locals EBITDAR -5%, Downtown -20%). Capital return of ~$180m and a 9.4% lower share count are doing the EPS work (adj. EPS $1.67, -2.9% YoY on adjusted earnings -12.6%), and leverage has drifted from 1.8x to 2.2x in two quarters as FanDuel-related tax payments, $650m of 2026 capex and $150m/qtr buybacks run ahead of cash generation.

summary: **Headline miss on revenue, in-line-to-slight-beat on profit.** Q3-26 revenue $990.5m (-1.4% YoY) vs ~$1.0bn consensus (Zacks: -1.3% surprise); adj. EBITDAR $319.6m (-0.7% YoY) vs $321.8m; adj. EBITDA $290.6m vs ~$287m StockStory consensus; adj. EPS $1.67 vs a $1.62-1.70 consensus range (Zacks $1.65). GAAP net income $124.9m / $1.71 vs $1.44bn / $17.81 a year ago, which included the $1.4bn after-tax gain on the FanDuel stake sale and $65.1m of impairments.

**Management's preferred framing is '+2% revenue / +1% EBITDAR' after stripping four items:** the Nov-2025 closure of Sam's Town Tunica, the 1-Aug-2026 sale of Sam's Town Shreveport to Bally's ($30m), a property-tax step-up at Kansas Star, and lower pass-through tax reimbursements in Online. We accept the first two as portfolio actions; the Kansas Star tax is a permanent cost and should not be adjusted out.

**The quarter's problem is one customer in one city.** Las Vegas Locals revenue -1.6% to $207.4m and adj. EBITDAR -5.1% to $87.4m (consensus $211.2m / $90.2m), margin 42.1% (-160bps YoY). Ex-Orleans and Suncoast the segment grew revenue and EBITDAR 3% (gaming +3.5%) at a 47% margin; the drag is 'destination' (non-local) business at the Orleans, which management says intensified in Q3 versus the ~$5m/qtr EBITDAR headwind disclosed in Q2, plus Suncoast construction.

**Downtown Las Vegas fell hardest:** revenue -10.9% to $47.4m, adj. EBITDAR -20.3% to $12.9m (consensus ~$14.3m), margin 27.1% (-320bps). Causes cited: destination softness, four storms hitting Hawaii in the last six weeks of the quarter, and a spike in Hawaiian airfares well above the ~20% national rise, now moderating. 9M Downtown EBITDAR -13.8%.

**Midwest & South remains the ballast:** revenue +0.3% to $540.5m, adj. EBITDAR flat at $201.6m (slight beat vs $200.0m), 37.3% margin. Adjusted for Tunica/Shreveport/Kansas Star tax, revenue +~3%, gaming revenue +>2%, EBITDAR +~$5m (+2.5%) at a 38% adjusted margin; 9M EBITDAR +2.9%. Management guided 2027 growth 'largely consistent' with 2026.

**Online and Managed both beat and guidance was steered to the top of the ranges.** Online adj. EBITDAR +15.9% to $10.9m (consensus $9.1m) on net online revenue +23.6% to $33.2m; Managed & Other +13.3% to $29.8m (consensus $28.1m) on Sky River management fees +16.4%. FY26 ranges unchanged at $35-40m (Online) and $113-117m (Managed), now 'high end' — implying ~$10m and ~$28m in Q4.

**Consumer read-through is two-speed:** core and retail customers growing, ADT/spend up mid-single digits, unrated play strong across Las Vegas and the regionals; softness confined to the low end of the database (gas prices/inflation). August was 'very soft' portfolio-wide, July good, September 'more normal' — the Q3 weakness is not purely a Las Vegas story.

**Operating cost control is the quiet positive.** Total opex -8.0% YoY (impairment lapping), but SG&A only +1.3% to $105.4m, corporate expense -4.0% to $29.4m (net corporate -$22.9m vs -$24.3m consensus), maintenance & utilities +1.5%. GAAP operating income +39% to $194.9m on the absence of last year's $65.1m impairment and a $24.2m gain on asset sales booked in 'project development, preopening and writedowns' (a $5.4m net credit).

**Below the line, D&A is the structural EPS headwind:** $91.3m vs $73.7m (+24% YoY; 9M +31%) as the capex programme (Cadence Crossing, Treasure Chest, Suncoast, hotel remodels) is capitalised. Adjusted earnings fell 12.6% to $121.7m while adj. EPS fell only 2.9% thanks to a 9.7% lower diluted share count (73.0m vs 80.9m).

**Capital return is on autopilot:** $164m of buybacks (~2.0m shares) plus $15m of dividends ($0.20/share paid 15 Oct) in Q3; ~$475m repurchased YTD; $387m left on the authorisation; target remains $150m/qtr, putting FY26 total return at >$680m (~$9.80/share on 70.7m shares). Share count 71.2m at quarter-end, 70.67m at 23 Oct.

**Balance sheet is loosening, deliberately.** Cash $297.2m, total debt ~$2.7bn ($1.0bn 4.75% notes due Dec-2027, $900m 4.75% notes due 2031, ~$800.9m of credit facility), net debt ~$2.4bn. Company-defined leverage 2.2x traditional / 2.7x lease-adjusted vs 1.8x / 2.4x at Q1-26. The entire credit facility ($800.9m) is classified as current because of a 1-Sep-2027 springing maturity tied to the 2027 notes; management will refinance 'later this year or 1H27'.

**Cash flow optics are distorted by the FanDuel tax bill.** 9M operating cash flow $313.4m vs $701.4m, after $364.2m of payments for transferable federal energy tax credits used to settle federal tax on the FanDuel sale ($73.8m in Q1, the balance in Q2). Underlying 9M OCF is ~$678m (our arithmetic) against 9M capex of $456.0m.

**Capex guidance trimmed to ~$650m from $650-700m:** $250m maintenance, $75m Orleans hotel remodel (1,800 rooms, done November), $50m growth (Cadence Crossing completion, Par-A-Dice design) and $275m for the Virginia resort (was $300m). Q3 capex $159m; implied Q4 ~$194m.

**Growth pipeline is land-based and 2027-28 weighted:** Norfolk, VA ($750m JV with the Pamunkey Tribe; 65k sq ft casino, 200 rooms) on time/budget for Nov-2027 opening, topping-out by year-end; Sky River phase 2 (300-room hotel, spa, event centre) 2028; Par-A-Dice (IL) land-based rebuild construction late 2027; Amelia Belle (LA) land-based conversion construction late 2027 subject to approvals; Orleans property-wide renovation starts early 2027 in back-of-house areas.

**Las Vegas outlook is 'less bad', not 'better':** Q4 destination trends guided to revert to the pre-Q3 run-rate (i.e. still negative), ~350 Orleans rooms back for weekends/NFR, Suncoast a 'very modest' Q4 contributor with 400+ rooms being remodelled through Q1-27, Cadence Crossing at full run-rate by Q1-27 (it contributed ~a third of the 3% ex-Orleans/Suncoast growth). 2027: 'modest growth' in LV Locals EBITDAR; ~50% margins remain the frame for the non-destination book.

**M&A posture unchanged but appetite 'as big as ever':** right asset, right price, stable tax/regulatory jurisdiction; management dismissed rumours, said compressed sector multiples neither raise nor lower appetite, and that low leverage exists precisely so buybacks and capex need not be sacrificed if a deal appears. Online M&A limited to 'bite-size' capability deals; supportive of iGaming legalisation (Virginia relevant given Norfolk). Pennsylvania skill-game removal should help Valley Forge (unquantified).

**Market reaction was muted but negative:** shares closed $72.27 on 22 Oct (+2.4% pre-print), fell ~2.9% after hours to ~$70.19, opened 23 Oct at $69.51 (-3.8%) and recovered to close $71.69 (-0.8%). Stock -15% YTD, 52-week range $65.00-91.41, market cap ~$5.1-5.2bn. Stifel cut its target to $80 from $92 (Hold) on 23 Oct.

**Thesis read-through:** the diversified, low-promo, locals/regional model is intact and the non-Las Vegas 85% of EBITDAR is growing low-single digits with margins held; but the Orleans/Downtown destination exposure (~15% of EBITDAR) has now been a negative for four-plus quarters and worsened in Q3, and the EPS algorithm is increasingly buyback-dependent while leverage drifts up into a 2027 refinancing at a higher coupon. We see FY26 adj. EBITDAR around $1.31-1.32bn (9M $987.5m + Q4E ~$325-335m) — flat-to-down ~2-3% on a reported basis.

segments.name: Las Vegas Locals
segments.headline: Two businesses in one segment: the locals book is growing 3% at 47% margins, but the Orleans' destination customer and Suncoast construction pulled EBITDAR down 5% YoY and 18% QoQ.
narrative: Revenue fell 1.6% YoY to $207.4m (-8.2% QoQ on normal summer seasonality) and adjusted EBITDAR dropped 5.1% to $87.4m, a 42.1% margin that is down ~160bps YoY and ~500bps from Q2's 47.1%. Both lines missed the three-analyst consensus ($211.2m revenue / $90.2m EBITDAR) by 1.8% and 3.1% respectively, and 9M EBITDAR is now down 5.7% to $293.8m. Management again split the segment in two: the Orleans, where the destination (non-local, drive-in and fly-in) customer softened further, and the Suncoast, in the final phase of its public-area renovation, versus everything else, which grew revenue and EBITDAR 3% with gaming revenue up 3.5% and margins of 47% — the same cadence as Q2 (+4% revenue) and the last several quarters. They conceded that Cadence Crossing, the Henderson casino that replaced Jokers Wild earlier this year, accounted for roughly a third of that 3%, so the same-store locals book is growing nearer 2%.

The destination drag is the number the market wanted and did not get. In Q2 the CFO sized it at ~$5m of EBITDAR per quarter, a level 'very consistent since Q3 of last year'; in Q3 it 'intensified' — July was fine, August weaker than anticipated, September better than August but not enough to offset — and they declined to quantify it, attributing the step-up partly to Q3 being the seasonally weakest Las Vegas quarter, which amplifies any demand shortfall. The Suncoast disruption, ~$3m in Q2, was 'a little less than expected' in Q3. They were explicit that there was no new promotional shock from the Strip or from the Palms/neighbouring locals properties — Strip room rates have been aggressive for more than two months and the Gold Coast and Orleans had stabilised against that pressure by 1H25 before destination softness took over — and that Boyd is choosing not to discount rooms at the Orleans to chase unprofitable volume. We read that as the right long-term decision and a reason the near-term revenue line will keep looking worse than peers who are discounting.

The locals case remains intact on the numbers they gave: core and retail segments grew, unrated play was strong, ADT/spend from core customers rose mid-single digits or better, with weakness confined to the low end of the database. Southern Nevada fundamentals were marshalled in support — population above 2.4m growing at twice the national rate, the second-highest job growth among the 30 largest metros over 12 months, wage growth near 6%. Ex-Orleans/Suncoast margins of 47% in the summer quarter match the Q3 prints of each of the last two years, with other quarters 'hovering around 50%', so the 50% margin frame management offered for 2027 is a non-summer number, not a step-up.

Outlook is sequenced rather than guided. The 1,800-room Orleans remodel completes in November, returning ~300-350 rooms that have been out of service daily for a year — not needed midweek, but useful for weekends, holidays and the National Finals Rodeo period; the Suncoast's 400+ rooms are remodelled through Q1-27, so Q4 is a 'very modest' contribution with the ramp coming in Q1-Q2 2027; Cadence Crossing reaches full run-rate around Q1-27; and the Orleans' property-wide renovation (framed as a 30-year 'major maintenance upgrade' rather than a fix for a specific product gap) starts early 2027 in areas not accessible to guests, so no disruption is guided for 2027. Q4 destination trends are guided to be 'similar to what we saw before Q3' — the CFO was careful to say not flat, not growing, not less bad — and 2027 LV Locals EBITDAR 'modest growth' depends on that holding. Management declined a request to break out the destination book separately, arguing it is a slice of one property; given it has dominated four consecutive calls, we think disclosure would help the multiple.

segments.name: Downtown Las Vegas
segments.headline: Hawaiian storms and airfares on top of market-wide destination softness: EBITDAR -20% YoY, the third straight quarter of double-digit declines.
narrative: Revenue fell 10.9% YoY to $47.4m (-9.0% QoQ) and adjusted EBITDAR dropped 20.3% to $12.9m against a ~$14.3m three-analyst consensus, with the margin at 27.1%, down ~320bps YoY and ~530bps QoQ. For the nine months EBITDAR is down 13.8% to $48.7m on revenue -6.8%, so Q3 was an acceleration of an existing trend rather than a new one. The segment is only ~4% of group EBITDAR, which is why it gets little airtime, but the margin decrement at this revenue scale is notable.

Management cited three overlapping drivers that they could not disaggregate: the same Southern Nevada destination softness affecting the Orleans; four storms hitting the Hawaiian Islands in the final six weeks of the quarter, which they described as unprecedented in that window; and a sharp spike in Hawaiian airfares in the second half of the quarter, well above the ~20% national rise, which has begun to moderate but remains elevated. Boyd's downtown properties (California, Fremont, Main Street Station) are disproportionately exposed to Hawaiian visitation through its Vacations Hawaii charter programme, so this is a known concentration risk that happened to bite in a seasonally weak quarter.

The Q2 commentary had been that core and Hawaiian play were 'consistent with recent quarters' with the softness confined to the broader downtown destination customer, so part of the Q3 step-down is weather and airfare that should mean-revert into the holiday season. The structural element — fewer and more price-sensitive visitors to Las Vegas — is the same issue as at the Orleans and will not be fixed by the calendar. We would not model a return to the 30%+ margins of 2024-25 until destination visitation stabilises; the near-term question is simply whether Q4 EBITDAR recovers to the mid-teens.

segments.name: Midwest & South
segments.headline: Flat reported, +2.5% adjusted EBITDAR at a 38% underlying margin; the regional portfolio is doing exactly what the model says it should, with 2027 guided to look like 2026.
narrative: Revenue rose 0.3% YoY to $540.5m and adjusted EBITDAR was flat at $201.6m, a modest beat against the ~$200.0m three-analyst consensus (revenue was slightly below the $543.7m estimate), with the margin steady at 37.3% (-10bps YoY, -20bps QoQ). Reported figures absorb the permanent closure of Sam's Town Tunica in November 2025, the 1 August sale of Sam's Town Shreveport to Bally's for $30m, and a step-up in property taxes at Kansas Star; adjusting for those, revenue grew nearly 3%, gaming revenue more than 2%, and EBITDAR rose ~$5m or ~2.5%, with an adjusted operating margin of 38% that management says is consistent with Q3 margins over the last several years. On a nine-month basis the segment is up 2.5% on revenue and 2.9% on EBITDAR at a 37.2% margin, the only property segment growing year-to-date.

The drivers were the same as in Las Vegas ex-Orleans: growth in play from core and retail guests, growth in unrated play, and returns on the capital that has gone into gaming floors, F&B and hotel rooms (Treasure Chest's land-based move, the Ameristar St. Charles hotel, floor refreshes). Management was candid that August was 'a very soft month' in the regionals as well, that July was good and September 'more normal', and that low-end database customers are showing inflation sensitivity; they see no distinction between South, East Coast and Midwest properties in consumer behaviour. They also attributed some of the 2026 strength to consumers staying closer to home and to tax-bill refunds earlier in the year, which is an honest acknowledgement that part of this year's comp was a tailwind.

The pipeline is entirely land-based and back-end loaded. The Norfolk, Virginia resort — a $750m development with the Pamunkey Indian Tribe (65k sq ft casino, 200 rooms, eight F&B outlets, serving 1.8m Hampton Roads residents and Virginia Beach visitors) — is on time and on budget for a November 2027 opening with topping-out by year-end, and will be a new property for this segment. Par-A-Dice in Illinois moves from a riverboat to an all-new single-level facility, in design with construction starting late 2027; Amelia Belle in Louisiana is to be converted to a land-based single-level floor, construction late 2027 subject to approvals. Pennsylvania's removal of unregulated skill games should lift Valley Forge, though management has nothing to report yet. Lattner, the small Illinois route business, will look at Chicago-area VGT licences but was explicitly described as not a needle-mover.

Guidance is that 2027 growth should be 'largely consistent' with 2026 — i.e. low-single-digit EBITDAR growth on the same-store base — with no sign in the databases that the trend is turning. Mechanically, Shreveport's absence will subtract from reported revenue and EBITDAR through Q2-27, the Kansas Star tax step-up is permanent, and preopening costs for Virginia will build through 2027 (reported below EBITDAR). We would model reported Q4-26 segment EBITDAR in the $195-200m range (estimate), allowing for Shreveport and normal Q4 seasonality.

segments.name: Online (Boyd Interactive + market access)
segments.headline: First clean post-FanDuel comparison: net online revenue +24%, EBITDAR +16% to $10.9m, FY26 guidance steered to the top of $35-40m.
narrative: Reported segment revenue fell 6.7% YoY to $154.5m, but $121.2m of that is zero-margin pass-through reimbursements from market-access partners (-12.6%, reflecting lower tax pass-throughs after the FanDuel restructuring), so the economically relevant line is net online revenue, which rose 23.6% to $33.2m (+4.4% QoQ). Adjusted EBITDAR grew 15.9% to $10.9m against a $9.1m consensus, a ~33% margin on net revenue (35% a year ago, as the mix shifts toward Boyd Interactive's own B2C/B2B activity from pure market-access fees). Management flagged Q3 as the first quarter since the July-2025 sale of the 5% FanDuel stake (for $1.76bn) to offer a comparable year-over-year read, which explains why 9M EBITDAR is down 45.7% to $29.9m — the 1H25 base still carried the old FanDuel market-access economics.

Boyd Interactive (the Stardust brand in New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Ontario, plus a B2B platform) delivered 'double-digit revenue and EBITDAR growth' again, driven by online casino. Management described the business as very efficient, with customer-acquisition costs they are comfortable with and no need to 'juice' marketing — a deliberate contrast with peers' spend-led strategies, which they said they will not replicate. FY26 segment EBITDAR guidance of $35-40m (raised by $5m at Q2) was left unchanged but 'directed toward the high end'; with 9M at $29.9m that implies ~$10m in Q4, roughly flat sequentially.

Strategically, management is supportive of properly regulated and taxed iGaming anywhere in the US — Virginia is the obvious live question given Norfolk — and would decide brand (Stardust or others) case by case. Online M&A is on the table but only for 'bite-size' capability deals that add something Boyd cannot build, assessed on the same return hurdles as land-based deals. Third-party market-access agreements continue to contribute at a level consistent with 2H25. This remains a small (~3% of group EBITDAR) but genuinely growing and capital-light line; the pass-through revenue line will keep flattering or distorting the reported segment number and should be ignored.

With 9M at $29.9m, that implies ~$10m in Q4, roughly flat sequentially.

segments.name: Managed & Other (Sky River, Lattner)
segments.headline: Sky River's phase-1 expansion is paying through: fees +16%, EBITDAR +13% to $29.8m, FY26 guidance to the high end of $113-117m; phase 2 (hotel) lands in 2028.
narrative: Revenue rose 13.3% YoY to $40.6m, with management fees from Sky River Casino (Wilton Rancheria, northern California) up 16.4% to $27.6m, and adjusted EBITDAR grew 13.3% to $29.8m against a $28.1m consensus, a ~73% margin. Sequentially the segment eased 3% from Q2's $30.7m, which management had pre-flagged as elevated following the opening of the first expansion phase (400 additional slots and a 1,600-space garage). Nine-month EBITDAR is up 11.7% to $88.9m, the fastest-growing line in the group.

Guidance of $113-117m for FY26 (raised $3m at Q2) is unchanged but steered to the high end, implying ~$28m in Q4 — flat sequentially, consistent with the expansion having reached run-rate. The next leg is phase 2: a 300-room hotel, three F&B outlets, a full-service spa and an entertainment/event centre, due in 2028, which should lift the fee base again as Sky River converts from a day-trip to an overnight property. Lattner (the Illinois distributed-gaming route) sits in 'Other' and is well run but small; the Chicago-area VGT opportunity is being evaluated and was explicitly described as immaterial.

For modelling purposes this is a high-margin, zero-capex fee stream (Boyd does not consolidate Sky River), so each incremental dollar is close to free cash flow; the risk is simply the contract term and the tribe's own development decisions. At ~9% of group EBITDAR and growing double digits, it is an underappreciated contributor to the diversification argument management keeps making.

highlights.text: **Core customer intact across the portfolio (structural):** core and retail play grew, unrated play strong, ADT up mid-single digits; LV Locals ex-Orleans/Suncoast +3% revenue and EBITDAR (gaming +3.5%) at 47% margins; Midwest & South +~3% revenue / +2.5% EBITDAR adjusted at a 38% margin, 9M segment EBITDAR +2.9%.

**Online and Managed both beat and were steered to the top of guidance:** Online EBITDAR +15.9% to $10.9m (vs $9.1m consensus) on net online revenue +23.6%; Managed & Other +13.3% to $29.8m (vs $28.1m) on Sky River fees +16.4%. Combined ~$40m/qtr of capital-light EBITDAR growing double digits.

**Cost discipline held in a soft quarter:** SG&A +1.3%, corporate expense -4.0% (net corporate -$22.9m vs -$24.3m consensus), M&S margin flat at 37.3%, group adj. EBITDAR margin +20bps YoY to 32.3% despite the revenue miss. Management: 'nothing special… day-to-day combat' on opex.

**Capital return and share count:** ~$180m returned in Q3 ($164m buybacks, $15m dividends), ~$475m repurchased YTD, FY26 total >$680m (~$9.80/share); diluted share count -9.7% YoY, period-end 71.2m (-9.4%). $387m authorisation remaining; $150m/qtr target reiterated with history of leaning in on dislocation.

**Capex guide trimmed to ~$650m from $650-700m** (Virginia $275m vs $300m), with Norfolk on time/budget for Nov-2027 and no disruption guided at the Orleans in 2027 as the renovation starts in back-of-house areas.

**Sequencing of Las Vegas self-help is visible:** ~1,800 Orleans rooms back in November after 300+ out daily for a year, Suncoast public areas complete (guest response 'enthusiastic'), Cadence Crossing ahead of revenue expectations and at full run-rate by Q1-27, Pennsylvania skill-game removal a free option for Valley Forge.
**GAAP optics improve:** operating income +39% to $194.9m (lapping $65.1m impairment; $24.2m asset-sale gain), 9M interest expense -29% to $93.7m after FanDuel-funded debt paydown.

lowlights.text: **Las Vegas destination softness worsened, not eased:** LV Locals EBITDAR -5.1% YoY / -17.9% QoQ to $87.4m (3.1% below consensus), margin 42.1% (-160bps YoY); the ~$5m/qtr headwind disclosed at Q2 'intensified' in Q3 and was not quantified. Same narrative for 'three or four quarters'; Q4 guided only to revert to the prior (negative) trend.

**Downtown Las Vegas EBITDAR -20.3% to $12.9m, margin 27.1% (-320bps):** storms and Hawaiian airfares are one-off, but destination softness is the same market-wide problem and 9M segment EBITDAR is -13.8%.

**Revenue missed (~1.1-1.3% below ~$1.0bn) and adjusted earnings fell 12.6% to $121.7m;** adj. EPS -2.9% to $1.67 only because the share count is 9.7% lower. Group adj. EBITDAR is -2.9% for the nine months with margin -90bps; D&A +24% YoY is a growing structural drag on EPS as capex is capitalised.

**Leverage rising into a refinancing:** traditional leverage 2.2x (1.8x at Q1-26), lease-adjusted 2.7x (2.4x); net debt ~$2.4bn; $800.9m of credit-facility borrowings classified current because of a 1-Sep-2027 springing maturity tied to the $1.0bn 4.75% notes due Dec-2027. Refinancing at today's coupons is likely a ~$12-18m p.a. interest headwind (our estimate).

**Cash generation this year is thin on a reported basis:** 9M operating cash flow $313.4m (vs $701.4m) after $364.2m of energy-tax-credit payments for the FanDuel tax bill, against $456m capex and ~$475m buybacks; cash fell to $297.2m. Underlying OCF (~$678m) is fine, but FY26 free cash flow after $650m capex does not cover the $680m+ capital-return programme.

**August was 'very soft' everywhere, including Midwest & South,** and low-end database customers are showing inflation/gas-price sensitivity; management also credited part of 2026 regional strength to stay-close-to-home behaviour and tax refunds — tailwinds that may not repeat.

**Online reported revenue -6.7% and 9M Online EBITDAR -45.7%** as FanDuel market-access economics roll off; the segment is small (~3% of EBITDAR) and the headline line will stay noisy because of zero-margin pass-through reimbursements.

forecast.intro: Boyd does not issue group guidance, so the 'bridge' is segment-level and capital-allocation guidance. Nothing was cut: Online FY26 adj. EBITDAR stays $35-40m and Managed & Other $113-117m, but both are now explicitly 'high end' after Q3 beats (implying ~$10m and ~$28m in Q4). The one numerical change is capex, trimmed to ~$650m from $650-700m (Virginia $275m vs $300m; $250m maintenance; $75m Orleans rooms; $50m growth), implying ~$194m in Q4. Buybacks stay at $150m/qtr. For the property segments the 'guidance' is qualitative: Q4 Las Vegas destination trends similar to pre-Q3 (still negative), Suncoast a 'very modest' Q4 contributor ramping in Q1-Q2 2027, Cadence Crossing at full run-rate by Q1-27, LV Locals 'modest' EBITDAR growth in 2027 with ~50% non-summer margins ex the destination assets, and Midwest & South 2027 growth 'largely consistent' with 2026. The division that moved the needle this quarter was Las Vegas Locals (Orleans destination + Suncoast), with Downtown adding to the miss; Online, Managed and corporate costs offset about half of it.

bridge.title: Capital return / balance sheet
bridge.change: unchanged; leverage 2.2x/2.7x; refinance Dec-27 notes late-26/1H27

forecast.view: **Q4-26E (our estimates):** revenue ~$0.99-1.01bn (flat to -1% YoY as Shreveport/Tunica and lower pass-through reimbursements offset Cadence and Orleans rooms), adj. EBITDAR ~$325-335m built as LV Locals ~$98-102m (normal mid/high-teens sequential uplift off a depressed Q3, Suncoast minimal), Downtown ~$15-16m, Midwest & South ~$195-200m, Online ~$10m, Managed ~$28m, corporate ~-$24m. That puts **FY26E adj. EBITDAR at ~$1.31-1.32bn** (9M actual $987.5m + Q4E), down ~2-3% reported. Q4 adj. EPS ~$1.75-1.85 (EBITDAR less ~$29m rent, ~$92m D&A, ~$33m net interest, ~$9m SBC, ~24% tax, ~70.6m shares) → **FY26E adj. EPS ~$6.95-7.05**. **Margin:** group adj. EBITDAR margin ~32.5-33% for FY26, roughly 90bps below FY25's nine-month level; property margins hold (M&S ~37-38%, LV Locals back toward mid-40s in Q4) and the drag is mix (Downtown, Orleans) rather than cost creep. **Leverage direction is up:** Q4 OCF normalises (~$230-250m with no tax-credit payments) but ~$194m capex plus ~$165m of buybacks/dividends pushes net debt toward ~$2.5bn and traditional leverage to ~2.3x at year-end; through 2027, with Virginia's remaining spend, the Orleans renovation, Par-A-Dice/Amelia Belle pre-construction and $600m+ of annual returns, we expect 2.4-2.5x (lease-adjusted ~3.0x) before Norfolk contributes from 2028 — still comfortable, but the 'low-leverage optionality' argument is being spent. The $1.0bn 4.75% 2027 notes must be refinanced (or taken out with the facility) before the 1-Sep-2027 springing maturity; at a ~6-6.5% coupon that is a ~$12-18m annual EPS headwind (~$0.13-0.19/share). **2027 shape:** M&S low-single-digit growth, LV Locals modest growth contingent on destination stabilising, Online ~$45-50m and Managed ~$120m+ (our estimates), Downtown flat at best, Virginia preopening costs below EBITDAR in 2H27. **Swing factors:** the Orleans destination customer (every $1m/qtr of headwind is ~0.3% of group EBITDAR), Hawaiian airfares, the August-type consumer air-pocket at the low end, the refinancing coupon, and whether management leans harder into buybacks at ~$70 — history says they do.
watch: Q4 Las Vegas Locals EBITDAR: does the Orleans destination drag revert to the ~$5m/qtr run-rate, and does the segment print ≥$98m with the 1,800 Orleans rooms back for NFR/holidays?
Suncoast ramp: ~$3m/qtr of disruption to recover from Q1-27, with 400+ rooms out until then; LV Locals 2027 'modest growth' and ~50% non-summer margin claims.
Refinancing of the $1.0bn 4.75% notes due Dec-2027 (springing facility maturity 1-Sep-2027): timing, coupon, and whether the $800.9m current classification is cleared by year-end.
Leverage path vs the $150m/qtr buyback: 2.2x→~2.3x at YE26 and 2.4-2.5x through 2027 on our numbers; any M&A ('appetite as big as ever') would stack on top.
Downtown: Hawaiian airfare normalisation and storm recovery; whether Q4 EBITDAR recovers to the mid-teens or the destination component keeps margins below 30%.
Consumer: repeat of the August air-pocket, low-end database softness, and whether the 2026 stay-close-to-home/tax-refund tailwinds in Midwest & South fade in 2027.
Online: Q4 ~$10m delivery; Virginia iGaming legislation; any 'bite-size' Boyd Interactive M&A; continued decline in pass-through reimbursements distorting the reported line.

Pipeline execution: Norfolk topping-out by YE26 and Nov-2027 opening; Sky River phase 2 (2028); Par-A-Dice and Amelia Belle construction starts late 2027 and their capex envelopes; Pennsylvania skill-game removal uplift at Valley Forge.
